text:
Ryan Donato's biggest moment of the season came Nov. 12, when his overtime winner against Buffalo ended a six-game Chicago slide. On Saturday in Calgary he scored on a delayed penalty and, per Mark Lazerus of The Athletic, had a breakaway stopped by Wolf. That's his season in one night: chances, and only some of them going in.

He has 4 goals and 7 points in 23 games on 12:21 a night, and his own finishing is fine (4 goals on 4.4 expected goals). The problem is around him. The Blackhawks have scored 5.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice and get only 41.7% of the five-on-five expected goals. Evolving-Hockey had his linemates in the bottom 2% by impact last season, so his raw numbers undersell him.

What he brings is a heavy shot (86th percentile in top shot speed) and a habit Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking picked up: 22% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. His ice time is up over the last ten games. Our projection: 10 to 20 goals.
